title: How a Solar Panel Makes Electricity

endcard.line: Pictures: Dr. Chinchu C. (CC BY 4.0); Wikideas1 (CC0). Footage: CSU/CIRA and NOAA (public domain)

segments.say: Sunlight falls on a rooftop, and a fan in the room below starts to turn. Not one moving part made that happen.

anim.title: When light hits a cell
items: Some is absorbed: only this makes power

segments.say: When sunlight reaches a solar cell, some of it bounces off and some passes through. Only the light that is absorbed makes electricity.

anim.title: Inside the cell
items: Light is absorbed by a semiconductor
They gather at the front surface

segments.say: A cell is made of a semiconductor. Absorbed light knocks electrons free; they gather at the front surface, and metal contacts collect them as a current.
Many cells make a panel, also called a module. Panels wired together make an array, from a rooftop to a solar park.
There is one catch. Cells make direct current, but homes and the grid use alternating current. A box called an inverter converts one into the other.
Large solar farms are so big that weather satellites can see them flash in the sunlight.
For GS Three, remember the chain: light, free electrons, direct current, inverter, alternating current.

sources: US EIA, 'Photovoltaics and electricity': PV cells are made of semiconductor material; photons are reflected, pass through or are absorbed; absorbed energy dislodges electrons, which migrate to the front surface, creating a charge imbalance; conductors collect the current; cells make panels (modules), panels make arrays; PV cells produce direct current, and inverters convert it to alternating current used by the grid

quiz.q: Which sunlight makes electricity in a solar cell?

options: Turns the panel to face the Sun
quiz.why: Cells make direct current; inverters convert it to alternating current.

quiz.q: What is a group of solar panels wired together called?
quiz.why: Cells make panels (modules); panels make arrays.

reviewNote: All facts are from the US EIA photovoltaics page. 'Weather satellites can see them' is drawn from the CIRA/NOAA footage title itself; check the clip shows a solar farm glint before approval. The fan in the opening is an illustration, not a claim. Moving facts: none.
